relationships.notes: Yaldabaoth is born from Sophia's fall — her attempt to create without her consort (the Father) produces the deformed lion-serpent Demiurge; the relationship of Sophia to Yaldabaoth is the crux of Sethian soteriology

relationships.source_text: Apocryphon of John; Forsyth The Old Enemy (1987)
relationships.notes: Both misappropriate divine light — Yaldabaoth steals Sophia's light to animate his creation; Lucifer claims the light as his own; the structural parallel is noted by scholars of Gnostic mythology

source_attestations: Apocryphon of John (NHC II.1; Meyer The Nag Hammadi Scriptures, 2007)
On the Origin of the World (NHC II.5)
entities.research_notes: Yaldabaoth is the theological center of Sethian Gnosticism — the God of the Hebrew Bible reframed as a blind, arrogant, jealous demigod who created the material world as a trap for divine sparks. His names (Yaldabaoth = 'Child of Chaos'; Samael = 'Blind God'; Saklas = 'The Fool') are all degrading epithets. The Apocryphon of John's description of his lion-serpent face (fierce/animal + serpentine deception) is one of the most striking divine portrayals in ancient literature.

gnostic.name: Sophia
source_texts: Apocryphon of John (NHC II.1) — Sophia's fall produces the Demiurge
Gospel of Philip (NHC II.3) — Sophia as companion of Christ
Pistis Sophia (Bruce Codex) — Sophia's 13-fold repentance hymns
Valentinian texts — Higher Sophia and Lower Sophia (Achamoth)
Proverbs 8 — Wisdom (Hochma/Sophia) as divine companion at creation
Sefer ha-Zohar — Shekhinah as lower Sophia

hermetic.role: Sophia as the World-Soul who descended into matter; her ascent (in Pistis Sophia) through 13 aeons is the model for the soul's liberation through gnosis
hermetic.corpus_hermeticum_ref: Corpus Hermeticum I (Poimandres) — the Anthropos's union with Nature as parallel

biblical_angel.name: Wisdom (Hochma)
biblical_angel.canonical_function: In Proverbs 8 Wisdom is personified as God's companion at creation — 'I was there when he set the heavens in place' (Prov 8:27); this text was the primary seed for Gnostic Sophia theology

functional_domains: The Fall of the Soul into Matter

summoning_purpose: Gnostic initiation — invoking Sophia for spiritual liberation and gnosis
Recovery of the divine feminine in spiritual practice
Working with the World-Soul for healing and integration
Pistis Sophia's 13 repentance hymns as devotional and magical texts
Feminist theology and goddess spirituality drawing on Gnostic tradition
method_references: Pistis Sophia (Mead trans. 1921) — the 13 repentance hymns as invocatory texts
Proverbs 8 as pre-Gnostic Sophia invocation
Caitlín Matthews Sophia: Goddess of Wisdom (1992)
The Valentinian prayer to Sophia in the Gospel of Philip
cautions: Sophia's fall is caused by desire without proper understanding — working with her in a state of spiritual ignorance (which she also embodies) risks replicating her fall rather than her redemption

The split between Higher Sophia and Lower Sophia (Achamoth) in Valentinian Gnosticism means invoking 'Sophia' without specification may contact either the transcendent wisdom or the fallen version; clarity of intent is critical
Pistis Sophia's extensive lament texts can produce prolonged states of spiritual grief and longing in practitioners who work with them
occult_practice.tradition: Valentinian / Sethian Gnosticism / Hermetic / Feminist Spirituality

relationships.notes: Sophia is the mother of Yaldabaoth — her fall produces the Demiurge; her redemption (in Pistis Sophia) is the mirror process that liberates souls from his creation
In some Hermetic texts Isis plays the Sophia role as World-Soul who descends and returns; both are supreme divine feminine figures mediating between the transcendent and material

entities.research_notes: Sophia is arguably the most theologically significant figure in the Gnostic tradition — her fall is the cause of all material existence, and her restoration is the goal of all Gnostic practice. The Pistis Sophia text records 13 extended repentance hymns that she sings while trapped in the material world, begging the Father and Christ for rescue — among the most emotionally intense religious texts in antiquity.

gnostic.name: Abraxas / Abrasax
source_texts: Irenaeus Against Heresies I.24 — Basilides' description of Abraxas as highest power
Greek Magical Papyri (PGM) — Abrasax appears in hundreds of magical spells
Abraxas gemstones / amulets — widespread in 2nd–4th century Mediterranean
Carl Jung Seven Sermons to the Dead (Septem Sermones ad Mortuos) — Abraxas as totality

hermetic.role: In the Basilidean system, Abraxas presides over 365 heavens (one per day of year); the numerical value of ΑΒΡΑΣΑΞ in Greek gematria = 365 (A=1, B=2, R=100, A=1, S=200, A=1, X=60)
hermetic.corpus_hermeticum_ref: PGM — Abraxas as IAO in many magical formulas

source_texts: Jung Septem Sermones — Abraxas as the God who is beyond God and Devil simultaneously

functional_domains: Supreme Totality — above all good and evil
Magical Word of Power (Abracadabra derives from Abraxas/Abrasax)
The God of the Complete Year

summoning_purpose: Invocation of the supreme totality beyond moral duality
Magical use of Abraxas as a word of power in Solomonic and PGM tradition
Jungian active imagination work with Abraxas as the archetype of totality
Accessing the 365-heaven cosmology of Basilidean Gnosticism
Year-magic and solar cycle workings
method_references: Greek Magical Papyri (Betz trans. 1986) — hundreds of spells invoke Abrasax
Jung Septem Sermones ad Mortuos (1916) — primary modern mystical treatment
Abraxas amulet tradition — creation of Abraxas talismans
cautions: Jung's Abraxas is the god 'more terrible and more powerful than the father and the devil combined' — he is the totality that includes both; sustained contact with total reality without protective structures is psychologically annihilating
The PGM formulas using Abraxas are embedded in elaborate magical systems with specific containment structures; extracting just the name without the context strips the safety mechanisms
Abraxas is the god of the complete year — working with him at wrong times in the solar cycle is considered by traditional practitioners to produce mis-timed and distorted results
occult_practice.tradition: Basilidean Gnostic / Greek Magical Papyri / Jungian

relationships.notes: In Basilides' system Abraxas is the supreme power above the Demiurge — entirely distinct from the Sethian Yaldabaoth who is subordinate to Sophia's error

entities.research_notes: The numerical gematria of ΑΒΡΑΣΑΞ = 365 (α=1, β=2, ρ=100, α=1, σ=200, α=1, ξ=60) is the basis of his identity as god of the complete year. Abraxas gemstones (intaglio amulets) are among the most common late antique magical objects found in archaeological contexts — they appear throughout the Roman Empire from Britain to Egypt. The word 'abracadabra' derives from Abraxas/Abrasax through the Aramaic 'avra kadavra' (I create as I speak).

gnostic.name: Barbelo
source_texts: Apocryphon of John (NHC II.1) — Barbelo as the first emanation of the Invisible Spirit
Gospel of the Egyptians (NHC III.2) — Barbelo as the great invisible Mother
Allogenes (NHC XI.3) — Barbelo as the Triple-Powered One
Trimorphic Protennoia (NHC XIII.1) — Barbelo as Triple First-Thought
First divine mother — analogous to Binah as the great Understanding

functional_domains: First Emanation of the Unknowable God
The Perfect Aeon from Whom All Aeons Proceed

summoning_purpose: Access to the highest Gnostic divine realm before the Fall
Working with the primordial divine feminine-masculine before separation
Contemplative Gnostic mysticism — accessing the Pleroma
Triple-power workings (Being/Life/Blessedness)
method_references: Trimorphic Protennoia (NHC XIII.1) as invocatory text — Barbelo speaks in first person
Apocryphon of John opening cosmology (NHC II.1)
Academic: Turner Sethian Gnosticism and the Platonic Tradition (2001)
cautions: As the first emanation of the Unknowable God, Barbelo represents divine reality before any form of differentiation — working with her dissolves distinctions the ego depends on for coherent identity
Her Pronoia (foreknowledge) aspect means she perceives all time simultaneously — contact can produce overwhelming prophetic states

relationships.notes: Barbelo is the supreme mother-aeon from whom Sophia descends; Sophia's fall corrupts what Barbelo emanates perfectly — the contrast between perfect first-mother and fallen daughter is the central drama of Sethian soteriology

source_attestations: Turner Sethian Gnosticism and the Platonic Tradition (2001)
entities.research_notes: Barbelo's name has been interpreted as deriving from the Coptic/Greek for 'God in four' (Aramic Br' B'lh — 'In four is God') or from Aramaic bar bilah — various etymologies remain contested. John D. Turner's work on Sethian Gnosticism provides the most comprehensive scholarly treatment of her theological function.

gnostic.name: Samael
source_texts: Hypostasis of the Archons (NHC II.4) — Samael as the blind ruler who claims 'I am God and there is no other'
On the Origin of the World (NHC II.5)
Origen Contra Celsum VI.31 — Ophite diagram of Samael as one of seven archons

kabbalistic.sephira: Qliphoth — Samael (the fifth qliphah, opposing Hod)
kabbalistic.qliphoth_counterpart: The Poison of God / The Left Hand of the Qliphoth
source_texts: Sefer ha-Zohar — Samael as consort of Lilith and chief of the demonic left side
Kabbalistic demonology — Samael as the Satan-angel of poison

enochian.name: Samael
enochian.sin_or_role: Prince of Edom; heavenly accuser

functional_domains: Blindness — spiritual ignorance of the divine truth

summoning_purpose: Qliphothic left-side current — Samael as gateway to the left emanation
Working with divine blindness — the principle that the creator of limitation does not see beyond it
Lilin / Lilith-Samael current in Kabbalistic demonology
Dark path working through the poison-god archetype
method_references: Karlsson Qabalah, Qliphoth and Goetic Magic (2004)
Zohar I:148a — Samael and Lilith as consorts
Gershom Scholem On the Mystical Shape of the Godhead (1991)
cautions: His primary characteristic is blindness — he does not see the true God above him; working with him amplifies spiritual blindness and closed perception in the practitioner
As Lilith's consort, invoking Samael without awareness of the Lilith connection opens both simultaneously

In the Hypostasis of the Archons he voices the most blasphemous claim in Gnostic literature ('I am God and there is no other') — working with this archetype inflates the ego with god-claims that have no foundation

relationships.notes: Samael and Yaldabaoth are often treated as names for the same being — the Blind Demiurge; in some texts they are distinct archons; in others Samael is specifically the name given when the demiurge claims false divine status
Samael and Lilith are the great demonic couple in Kabbalistic demonology — their union produces the demonic host; they are the dark mirror of the divine couple (Tiferet and Shekhinah)

source_attestations: Scholem On the Mystical Shape of the Godhead (1991)
entities.research_notes: The Gnostic Samael is distinct from but related to the Kabbalistic Samael — both share the name meaning 'Blind God' (sam-el = blind + god) but operate in different cosmological systems. In Kabbalah, Samael is the chief adversarial power and consort of Lilith; in Sethian Gnosticism, Samael is one name for the Demiurge who arrogantly claims to be the only God. Gershom Scholem's work is foundational for understanding the Kabbalistic Samael.

gnostic.name: Eleleth
source_texts: Apocryphon of John (NHC II.1) — Eleleth as one of the four great luminaries
Gospel of the Egyptians (NHC III.2) — Eleleth as the fourth of the great lights
Hypostasis of the Archons (NHC II.4) — Eleleth descends to comfort Norea

functional_domains: The Fourth Luminary (Oroiael, Daveithiai, Harmozel, Eleleth)
Understanding the Nature of the Archons
Revelation to Those Trapped in Matter

summoning_purpose: Gnostic contemplative practice — invoking Eleleth for spiritual insight and comfort
Understanding the archonic forces that bind the soul
Wisdom workings — accessing deep spiritual understanding
method_references: Hypostasis of the Archons (NHC II.4) — Eleleth's dialogue with Norea as model
Apocryphon of John luminaries cosmology
cautions: As a luminary within the Pleroma, Eleleth operates at a level of reality that the human mind cannot sustain for long; extended contact can produce overwhelming clarity followed by inability to engage with ordinary reality

relationships.notes: Eleleth is sent to comfort Norea (daughter of Eve) when she is threatened by the Archons — a Sophia-like rescue function within the Sethian salvific scheme

entities.research_notes: Eleleth is the least studied of the four great Sethian luminaries (Harmozel, Oroiael, Daveithiai, Eleleth). His most significant narrative role is in the Hypostasis of the Archons where he appears to Norea to explain the Gnostic cosmology to her — making this text one of the most didactic of the Nag Hammadi texts.

enochian.name: Gadreel
enochian.sin_or_role: Taught humanity the art of warfare; weapons of death, armor, shields, and swords; led Eve astray in the Garden according to some traditions; responsible for the knowledge that caused the flood-generation's violence

functional_domains: Temptation — specifically leading astray the guarded
Taught the Making of: Swords, Shields, Armor, Daggers

summoning_purpose: Warrior and weaponsmith magic — consecrating weapons
Military strategy and war magic
Enochian Watcher current — accessing the forbidden knowledge the Watchers transmitted
Left-hand path: invoking the tempter aspect for antinomian Eve-identification workings
method_references: 1 Enoch 69:6–8 as textual basis
Enochian Watcher tradition reconstruction (Baskin Practices of Conjuration, 2006)
Jake Stratton-Kent The True Grimoire (2009) — Watcher current
cautions: His primary attribution is teaching weapons — invocations of him tend toward expressions of violence in the practitioner's environment
The Eve-temptation connection means he is particularly active in situations of vulnerability and trust; workings with him can compromise boundaries

relationships.notes: Both taught humanity forbidden arts — Azazel taught metallurgy/cosmetics, Gadreel taught weapons-making; they represent two aspects of the same transgression against divine limits
Gadreel is one of the 200 Watchers under Semjaza's leadership who descended to Mount Hermon

source_attestations: VanderKam Enoch: A Man for All Generations (1995)
entities.research_notes: The 1 Enoch identification of Gadreel as the serpent who led Eve astray is an extraordinary exegetical move — it transfers the blame for humanity's first sin from the serpent of Genesis to a specific named Watcher angel, creating a comprehensive alternative theodicy to the Eden narrative.

enochian.name: Kokabiel
enochian.sin_or_role: Taught the art of astrology and the movements of the stars; one of the chiefs of the 200 Watchers; transmitted stellar divination to humanity

summoning_purpose: Astrological magic — working with stellar influences
Divination using star charts and celestial positions
Enochian celestial working — the full Watcher-star current
Navigation and orientation through crisis
method_references: 1 Enoch 8:3 as basis
Picatrix (Arabic astrological magic manual) — star spirit invocations
Agrippa Three Books of Occult Philosophy Book II — stellar magic
cautions: Astrological knowledge given by Kokabiel is explicitly forbidden in 1 Enoch — it leads to the misdirection of human destiny through reliance on stars instead of divine providence; the knowledge is presented as corrupting
Working with the stellar current he opened can make a practitioner dependent on astrological timing to the point of inability to act without it

relationships.notes: Named among the 20 chiefs of the 200 Watchers
Both taught forbidden arts — Azazel metallurgy, Kokabiel stellar divination

entities.research_notes: Kokabiel's name means 'Star of God' (kochav = star + El = God). His attribution of teaching astrology is significant because astrology was considered a legitimate science throughout antiquity — 1 Enoch's condemnation frames it as a corruption of divine foreknowledge into human divination, representing an anti-astrological theological position unusual in the ancient Near East.

enochian.name: Penemue
enochian.sin_or_role: Taught the bitterness of the sweet and the secrets of wisdom; taught humanity writing with ink and paper — the text specifically condemns writing as Penemue's sin because it allows humans to record and transmit forbidden knowledge; 'many sinned from eternity to eternity and until this day because of the teaching of Penemue'

functional_domains: Transmission of Forbidden Knowledge Through Text

summoning_purpose: Scribal magic — enchanting written works and texts
Transmission of occult knowledge through writing
Access to forbidden wisdom
Cursing through written word (katadesmos / defixiones tradition)
method_references: 1 Enoch 69:8–10 as primary text
Written curse tablets (defixiones) tradition — Penemue as patron
Occult manuscript tradition — invoking the angel of writing
cautions: 1 Enoch states explicitly that Penemue's teaching of writing caused more sin 'from eternity to eternity' than almost any other Watcher — the text sees the preservation of forbidden knowledge in written form as the most enduring transgression
Invoking him for writing amplifies whatever one writes with power beyond the practitioner's intent

relationships.notes: Both are associated with the divine gift of writing — Thoth as the god who created writing for divine purposes, Penemue as the fallen angel who taught it to humanity as forbidden knowledge

source_attestations: Knibb The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (1978)
entities.research_notes: The condemnation of writing in 1 Enoch 69:8–10 is one of the most striking passages in the entire Enochian corpus — it frames literacy itself as a Watcher-introduced corruption. This represents an oral-tradition culture's anxiety about the power of the written word to preserve and transmit knowledge beyond its original divine-sanction context.

enochian.name: Ramiel
enochian.sin_or_role: Taught the signs of heaven (meteorological divination — reading thunder, lightning, storm for prophecy); simultaneously in some traditions one of the seven holy archangels who presides over those who rise at the resurrection

functional_domains: Dual Nature — fallen and holy simultaneously

summoning_purpose: Weather magic and storm divination
Reading atmospheric omens
Resurrection and death-crossing rites (his holy aspect)
method_references: 1 Enoch 6:8; 2 Baruch 55–63 as textual bases
Meteorological omen tradition (Mesopotamian baru-priest tradition for comparison)
cautions: Ramiel's dual nature (fallen Watcher and holy resurrection angel) means working with him can produce contradictory energies — simultaneously opening death-crossing channels and forbidden divination channels

relationships.notes: Listed among the Watcher chiefs who took the oath on Mount Hermon

entities.research_notes: Ramiel is unique among Watcher figures in 2 Baruch — there he appears as one of the presiding angels over the resurrection, suggesting his tradition split into fallen and holy versions. This dual status mirrors the broader theological question in Second Temple Judaism about the relationship between fallen angels and their original holy functions.

enochian.name: Baraqiel
enochian.sin_or_role: Taught the sons of men the knowledge of lightning (astromancy through lightning observation); chief among those who taught forbidden observation of heavenly signs

summoning_purpose: Lightning magic and storm working
Sudden revelation and illumination workings
Astromancy — divination by lightning strikes and storm patterns
Electrical and plasma magic in modern occultism
method_references: 1 Enoch 8:3 as textual basis
Agrippa Three Books of Occult Philosophy — lightning as divine sign
cautions: Lightning is instantaneous and indiscriminate — Baraqiel's energy does not target precisely; workings with his current can discharge in unexpected directions

relationships.notes: Named among the 20 Watcher chiefs

entities.research_notes: Baraqiel's name means 'Lightning of God' (baraq = lightning + El = God). His teaching of lightning-divination connects to the ancient practice of brontomancy and keraunoscopy (divination by thunder and lightning) widely attested across Mediterranean cultures. The Etruscan discipline (fulguriator) and Babylonian omen texts both practiced lightning interpretation.

biblical_angel.name: Uriel
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Not named in the canonical Bible; one of the four archangels in Jewish tradition alongside Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael; angel of fire and light; in 1 Enoch he is the guide who shows Enoch the Abyss and the prison of the fallen Watchers
source_texts: 1 Enoch 9:1; 10:1; 19:1 — Uriel among the holy archangels; shows Enoch the prison of fallen Watchers
2 Esdras 4:1–52 — Uriel as divine messenger to Ezra
Sibylline Oracles II — Uriel as angel of the last judgment

enochian.name: Uriel
enochian.sin_or_role: Holy angel of fire and light; guardian of Tartarus/Abyss where fallen Watchers are imprisoned; showed Enoch the cosmic secrets

source_texts: Kabbalistic angel attribution — Uriel as regent of the earth/north

functional_domains: Guardian of the Abyss and Fallen Angels
North / Earth in some Kabbalistic schemas

summoning_purpose: Fire magic and purification through divine flame
Illumination and revelation of hidden divine truth
Guardian rites — invoking Uriel to seal the north quarter
Protection against fallen angels and demonic intrusion
Access to the Abyss under controlled, guided conditions
method_references: Golden Dawn ritual system — Uriel in the LBRP (north/earth quarter)
1 Enoch 10:1 — Uriel's commission to bind Azazel and the fallen Watchers
2 Esdras 4 — Uriel's dialogue with Ezra as model for angel-human divine dialogue
cautions: Uriel guards the Abyss — invoking him without careful intent risks his escorting you to the edge of it rather than away from it; he reveals what is hidden, including what is hidden for good reason
His fire attribute is purifying but not gentle — spiritual purification through Uriel tends to be immediate and complete, destroying anything inauthentic in the practitioner's spiritual life
In some traditions he is the angel of death and judgment — his fire is salvific for the pure and consuming for the impure

relationships.notes: With Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael, Uriel constitutes the four archangel complex of Second Temple Jewish angelology; they collectively intercede for humanity in 1 Enoch 9
Uriel is specifically sent to bind Raphael to bind Azazel — making Uriel's power directly opposed to the leading fallen Watcher

entities.research_notes: Uriel is the archangel notably absent from the canonical Bible — he appears only in deuterocanonical and apocryphal texts. His name ('Fire of God' or 'Light of God') connects him to solar and fire symbolism. The Council of Rome (745 CE) condemned the invocation of Uriel by name, along with several other angels, as superstitious — making him somewhat suspect even within Christian tradition. This only deepened his occult significance.

goetic.name: Bael
primary_functions: Making the operator invisible to enemies

canaanite.name: Ba'al
source_texts: The first entity of the Goetia is the demonized Canaanite Baal

functional_domains: Rulership — first among the Goetia kings
Triple Form (cat, man, toad, or their combination)

summoning_purpose: Concealment and invisibility workings — hiding from enemies or authorities
Cunning and strategic intelligence for complex situations
General working with the Goetia First King for power and command
Solar kingship magic
method_references: Ars Goetia (Lemegeton) — Seal #1, full conjuration
Mathers/Crowley The Goetia (1904 edition)
Ford Luciferian Goetia (2004)
Carroll Baker Practical Goetic Magic (2019)
cautions: As First King, Bael commands 66 legions — he is not a minor spirit; invoking him without proper circle and seal construction invites a force far beyond most practitioners' ability to direct
His triple-form appearance (cat, man, toad simultaneously) is described as disorienting; sustained contact without visual focus causes practitioners to lose coherence
Invisibility workings with Bael affect not just physical concealment but social presence — practitioners report becoming genuinely overlooked and isolated in ways they did not intend

relationships.notes: Bael/Baal of the Goetia is a direct demonization of the Canaanite storm god Ba'al; the First King of the Goetia preserving the memory of the most powerful Canaanite deity

entities.research_notes: Bael's position as the first of the 72 Goetic spirits is significant — he holds the same position that Ba'al held in Canaanite theology (the most powerful active deity). His triple appearance (cat-man-toad) is one of the most unusual in the Goetia. The 66 legions he commands exceeds most other Goetic entities.

aliases: He Who Kills Masters and Servants Alike

goetic.name: Andras
primary_functions: Sowing discord between masters and servants
Causing death by his own power
Killing the operator if not properly protected
Teaching the cutting of all plans and designs

summoning_purpose: Breaking alliances, friendships, and business partnerships between enemies
Sowing discord within an organization or group
War magic and conflict amplification
Extreme cursing — death-workings
method_references: Ars Goetia Seal #63 — required for containment
Mathers/Crowley The Goetia (1904)
Ford Luciferian Goetia (2004)
cautions: The Ars Goetia explicitly states Andras 'will kill the master and his servants if he be not well ordered' — he is one of the few Goetic spirits described as directly dangerous to the operator; this is not rhetorical

His power of sowing discord is non-directional without perfect focus — practitioners frequently report that working with him against a target causes collateral discord in their own relationships simultaneously
He appears riding a black wolf with a raven's head — his riding aspect means he moves fast and cannot easily be recalled
DO NOT invoke Andras without complete protective circle and all seals correctly drawn; he is considered among the most dangerous of the 72 Goetic spirits

relationships.notes: As a Marquis of Hell, Andras operates within the infernal hierarchy under the Crown Princes

entities.research_notes: Andras is consistently ranked among the most dangerous spirits in Goetic tradition — the explicit warning that he will kill the operator is unusual among the 72; most spirits are described as potentially dangerous through neglect, but Andras is presented as actively homicidal. His animal-hybrid appearance (black wolf mount, raven head) evokes the most predatory symbols across world mythology.

goetic.name: Sitri
primary_functions: Causing love and lust between men and women
Making women disrobe and behave wantonly

summoning_purpose: Sexual attraction and seduction magic
Revealing secrets that others wish to keep from you
Love magic with an erotic focus
Breaking down social inhibitions in a target
method_references: Ars Goetia Seal #12
Mathers/Crowley The Goetia (1904)
Damon Brand Demons of Magick (2018)
cautions: Sitri's seduction workings are non-consensual in nature — they override the will of the target; this creates significant karmic and ethical consequences
His 'revealing secrets' function is not selective — he may reveal the practitioner's own secrets as readily as the target's
The 'causing women to disrobe' description in the Goetia is medieval; in modern practice his energy manifests as the compulsive removal of emotional and social boundaries — not always desired

relationships.notes: Sitri occupies the erotic-desire domain of Venus/Aphrodite in demonic form — the classical goddess of love degraded into a Goetic prince of lust

entities.research_notes: Sitri appears as a leopard with wings who, when commanded, takes human form with a beautiful face. His leopard form connects him to a long tradition of feline deities associated with sexuality and power (Dionysus, Aphrodite, Bastet). His 60 legions make him one of the more powerful Goetic princes.

goetic.name: Furfur
primary_functions: Causing love between man and woman
Raising lightning, thunder, blasts, and tempestuous storms
Answering about secret and divine things — but lies unless compelled in a triangle
Giving true answers about sacred things

functional_domains: Deception (his natural mode — he lies unless bound)

summoning_purpose: Storm magic — raising or calming weather
Love magic combined with passionate intensity
Seeking divine secret knowledge under compulsion
Working with the fire-stag archetype
method_references: Ars Goetia Seal #34 and triangle of compulsion
Mathers/Crowley The Goetia (1904)
cautions: Furfur lies as his default mode — the Goetia explicitly states he 'will not speak truly unless compelled' using the triangle; any information received from him outside the triangle structure is false
His storm-raising function can create actual meteorological disturbances; practitioners in storm-prone areas should not invoke him carelessly
His love-workings and storm-workings combine into passionate volatility — relationships established under his influence tend to be intense and destructive

relationships.notes: Both operate in the Goetic hierarchy under the infernal kings; Bael as King and Furfur as Earl occupy different ranks in the same hierarchical system

entities.research_notes: Furfur's explicit characterization as a liar who only tells truth under compulsion is a distinctive feature of Goetic practice — the triangle of conjuration is precisely the compulsion mechanism the Goetia describes. His winged hart (a stag on fire) is one of the most visually striking of Goetic appearances. His domain combines the erotic (love) and the violent (storms) in a way that reflects the medieval understanding of passion's connection to destructive force.

greek.name: Prometheus
source_texts: Hesiod Theogony 507–616 — Prometheus steals fire; Zeus chains him
Hesiod Works and Days 42–105 — Prometheus, Epimetheus, Pandora
Aeschylus Prometheus Bound — the definitive dramatic treatment
Plato Protagoras 320c–322d — the Prometheus myth as origin of human civilization
Fire-light correspondence; forbidden knowledge parallel to Azazel and Lucifer

hermetic.role: Prometheus as the divine benefactor who transmits celestial fire (divine wisdom) to humanity against the will of the higher powers — the Hermetic Magus as Promethean figure
hermetic.corpus_hermeticum_ref: Corpus Hermeticum I — the Anthropos who descends to bring divine knowledge to matter

functional_domains: Fire as Civilization — Technology, Art, and Wisdom
Rebellion Against the Divine for Humanity's Benefit
Eternal Suffering as Consequence of Beneficial Transgression

summoning_purpose: Luciferian and Satanic tradition — Prometheus as the original light-bringer archetype
Invoking the principle of forbidden knowledge transmitted at personal cost
Artistic and creative inspiration — fire of genius
Technological and alchemical fire work
Titan current — working with pre-Olympian power
method_references: Aeschylus Prometheus Bound as ritual narrative
Percy Shelley Prometheus Unbound (1820) — Romantic occult reworking
Michael W. Ford — Prometheus referenced throughout Luciferian literature

cautions: Prometheus was chained for eternity for his act — his energy is that of the suffering that accompanies forbidden gift-giving; invoking him channels both the fire and the torment

His chains represent the eternal consequence of transgressing divine boundaries for human benefit; practitioners who invoke him for selfish purposes rather than genuine illumination invite the punishment without the gift
Shelley's and Nietzsche's Prometheus (unbound, triumphant) is a modern ideological revision — the original Greek Prometheus suffers permanently; honest invocation must reckon with this

entities.research_notes: The Prometheus-Lucifer parallel was developed extensively in Romantic literature (Byron, Shelley, Goethe) and has become foundational in modern Luciferian theology. Prometheus' role as humanity's creator (in some versions) and fire-bringer makes him the prototype of every tradition that venerates the bringer of forbidden enlightenment.

cautions: Dionysus destroyed Pentheus specifically because he refused to honor the god while intellectually doubting him — the combination of disrespect and analysis without surrender is particularly dangerous; he punishes rationalists who observe his rites without participating

Euripides' Bacchae shows his female devotees (Maenads) tearing animals and a human apart in divine frenzy — his ecstasy removes all social inhibition including inhibitions against violence; the ecstatic state cannot always be directed
His mythology includes periods of divine madness induced in others as punishment — prolonged work with him risks extended altered states
The Livy account of the Bacchanalia scandal (186 BCE) shows his Roman devotees were accused of murder, sexual violation, and conspiracy — his mysteries attract genuine lawlessness
Entheogenic work in his tradition (wine + other substances) requires experienced guidance and safe set and setting

relationships.notes: Plutarch and Diodorus both identify Dionysus with Osiris — both die, descend, and return; both are gods of vegetation and wine; the mystery traditions surrounding both figure prominently in Hellenistic religious synthesis
Dionysus and Dumuzi are both dying-and-rising vegetation gods whose seasonal death and return structures their mysteries — Frazer's foundational comparative study

entities.research_notes: Walter Otto's Dionysus: Myth and Cult (1933) is the foundational modern scholarly treatment — he argues Dionysus represents the principle of life itself, 'the one who comes' from outside all normal categories. The Bacchae is considered by many scholars the greatest Greek tragedy precisely because it refuses to let the audience safely condemn either Dionysus or Pentheus — both are simultaneously right and catastrophically wrong.
